title: Security and privacy
description: Review who can reach the changed systems, which data they can see and which controls need evidence.
questions: Which actors, permissions and data classes does the change affect?
What controls already cover the new data path, and who owns them?
What verification should a reviewer see before approving the change?

sources.title: NIST SP 800-218, Secure Software Development Framework 1.1
CNIL, Guide de la sécurité des données personnelles

specialists.title: Application security reviewer
specialists.focus: Trace authorization from each affected entry point to the resource it protects. Verify the expected access rules for users, services and background jobs.

specialists.title: Privacy engineer
specialists.focus: Map personal and sensitive data to its purpose, recipients and retention. Flag fields or transfers that require the data owner's decision.

specialists.title: Software supply chain reviewer
specialists.focus: Review changed dependencies, identity scopes and artifact provenance. Determine whether the release evidence applies to the exact build under review.

specialists.title: Security control owner
specialists.focus: Match the proposed change to approved controls, available evidence and open exceptions. Identify who can accept a residual risk and when it must be revisited.

evidence: An approved data flow showing the affected actors, systems, trust boundaries, sensitive fields and external recipients.
Access matrix for the changed resources, with results of approved defensive checks for permitted access, denied access and isolation where relevant.
Data owner's decision on purpose, retention, deletion and disclosure, including copies in logs, caches and third-party services.
Changed dependency inventory and relevant advisory, credential or build-provenance review tied to the release revision.
List of applicable controls and open findings, with evidence, owner and approved exception details where available.
challenge: Which affected entry point or background worker can reach the data under a different identity from the main request?
How does the approved role or tenant change take effect for already active sessions and cached access decisions?
Which copies of the data survive the primary deletion flow, and who owns their retention?
Does the evidence cover the exact revision and access scope that will ship?
decision_criteria: Approve the reviewed scope when the asset owner can verify access boundaries and the defensive checks cover the affected roles and resources.
Hold exposure of the changed path when authority, data handling or a required control remains unresolved.
Route exceptions to the named risk owner and record accepted scope, expiration and follow-up evidence.
Describe which controls were reviewed and which evidence remains outstanding when reporting approval.
